name: Statue of Ramses II with Nefretari
description: A grand and historically significant statue depicting the pharaoh Ramesses II alongside his Great Royal Wife, Nefertari. Its monumental scale and fine craftsmanship make it a striking example of ancient Egyptian royal art.
address: PM94+GX8, Karnak, Luxor, Luxor Governorate

name: Valley of the Kings
description: The legendary royal necropolis where pharaohs of the New Kingdom were laid to rest in elaborately decorated tombs carved deep into the cliffs. Walking through its extraordinary painted corridors and chambers is an unforgettable, must-do experience in Luxor.
address: Luxor, Luxor Governorate 1340420

name: First Pylon
description: The massive First Pylon of Karnak, actually the last of the temple's ten pylons, built during the 30th Dynasty. Its towering, unfinished gateway offers an awe-inspiring introduction to the vast temple complex beyond.
address: PM94+PQ3, Luxor City, Luxor, Luxor Governorate

name: Banana Island Sara
description: A relaxing green retreat reached by a peaceful, scenic boat ride along the Nile, planted with banana trees and tropical greenery. Fresh fruit and especially good sugar-cane juice make it an enjoyable half-day escape from the city.
address: MJJC+Q2, Al Aqaletah, Al Qarna, Luxor Governorate 1344552

name: Tombs of the Nobles
description: A fascinating, less-crowded collection of tombs belonging to the officials and nobles of ancient Thebes, with tickets covering several tombs. Beautifully decorated and quieter than the royal valleys, they reward visitors with time and energy to explore.
address: PJJ5+8P4, Al Qarna, Luxor Governorate 1340420

name: First Pylon Luxor Temple
description: The monumental gateway to Luxor Temple, built by Ramesses II and standing some 24 meters high, decorated with sunken reliefs of the Battle of Kadesh. Flanked by colossal statues, it forms a breathtaking, iconic entrance to the temple.
address: PJ2Q+4VF, Luxor City, Luxor, Luxor Governorate 1362501

name: Colossi of Memnon
description: Two gigantic seated statues of Amenhotep III, each carved from a single block of stone, standing sentinel on the West Bank. Impressive in scale and set in their original location, they make a memorable, free stop on the way to the West Bank sites.
address: Al Bairat, Al Qarna, Luxor Governorate 1341703

name: Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut
description: The magnificent terraced mortuary temple of Hatshepsut, the queen who became pharaoh, set dramatically against the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari. Its striking colonnaded design and grand setting make it one of Luxor's most iconic monuments.
address: Al Qarna, Luxor Governorate 1340420

name: Tomb of Neferrenpet
description: A tomb in the Theban Necropolis belonging to the ancient official Neferrenpet, part of the West Bank's rich burial grounds. A quieter stop for those keen to explore beyond the most famous tombs.
address: El-Khokha, 10 km ovest, Luxor Governorate

name: Imhotep Alabaster Luxor
description: An alabaster souvenir shop where staff explain the traditional carving techniques in detail and offer a warm welcome with a drink. High-quality limestone and alabaster pieces make it a rewarding stop for handmade craft.
address: Al Qarnah, Luxor, Luxor Governorate 1341743

name: El - Souk
description: Luxor's lively main bazaar, a roughly two-kilometer stretch of local shops selling everything from handmade jewelry to spices and souvenirs. Bustling and colorful, it's a vibrant place to browse and experience the city's market atmosphere.
address: Girls School area, Luxor City, Luxor Governorate

name: Luxor Tourist Market
description: A bustling market packed with Egyptian souvenirs of all kinds, from clothing to crafts. Good merchandise and friendly sellers make it worth a visit, with a bit of good-natured bargaining part of the experience.
address: Abd El-Hameed Taha, Luxor City, Luxor, Luxor Governorate 1362422

name: Luxor Museum
description: A compact but beautifully curated museum showcasing some of the finest artifacts from Luxor's archaeological sites, including statues, mummies, and funerary objects. Its top-quality, well-displayed collection makes it a rewarding hour or two.
address: PJ5V+2RV, Kornish Al Nile, Luxor City, Luxor, Luxor Governorate 1362503

name: Mummification Museum
description: A small, well-presented museum offering a clear, fascinating insight into the ancient art of mummification, with tools, diagrams, and preserved specimens. Conveniently located on the corniche, it's a cool, engaging break from the sites outside.
address: Nile Corniche, Luxor City, Luxor Governorate

name: Karnak
description: One of the largest and most awe-inspiring temple complexes in the world, built and expanded over many centuries. Wandering among its colossal pylons, towering columns, and intricate carvings is an unforgettable highlight of any visit to Luxor.
address: Karnak, Luxor, Luxor Governorate

name: Luxor Temple
description: A magnificent temple in the heart of the city, especially atmospheric when illuminated at night, featuring a massive pylon, colonnaded courts, and a grand hypostyle hall. Its central location and striking scale make it an essential Luxor experience.
address: Luxor City, Luxor, Luxor Governorate 1362501

name: Precinct of Amun-Re
description: The vast main precinct at the heart of the Karnak complex, dedicated to the god Amun-Re and among the most jaw-dropping ancient sites in Egypt. Its immense halls and towering columns make it a truly awe-inspiring place to linger.
address: PM95+46C, Karnak, Luxor, Luxor Governorate

name: Temple Of Khonsu
description: A beautifully preserved, often-overlooked temple within the Karnak complex, dedicated to the moon god Khonsu. Tucked toward the edge of the site, it rewards those who find it with a quieter, more intimate experience.
address: PM84+J8F, Luxor City, Luxor, Luxor Governorate

name: The Michael Angel Church, Luxor
description: A grand Coptic Orthodox cathedral in Luxor, one of the largest in the region with a soaring tower and space for thousands of worshippers. Welcoming and spiritually significant, it's a notable landmark of the city's Christian community.
address: PJ2W+296, Al Saha, Luxor City, Luxor, Luxor Governorate 1362454
